the antioxidant alpha-lipoate at clinically relevant doses inhibits PMA-induced adhesin expression and function via specific redox-sensitive mechanisms.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

alpha-lipoate alone, and in combination with alpha tocopherol, inhibits PMA-induced adhesiveness in human EC cells and the adhesion of Jurka T-cells to EC cells by regulating adhesion molecule expression.
the regulation of adhesin molecule expression and cell adhesion processes by alpha-lipoic acid and alpha-tocpherol is not mediated by transcription or PKC dependent mechanisms.

The main takeaway from our work is that
low concentration of antioxidants can be used to regulate adhesion molecule expression, function and cell-cell adhesions.
low doses of clinically safe antioxidant, alpha-lipate, can regulate agonist-induced expression of adhesion molecules and cell-cell adhesions.
the combination of alpha-lipoate plus alpha-tocopherols may provide a new approach for the prevention of inflammatory disease.
